faq_items.question: When should I start my Christmas planning checklist?
faq_items.answer: Start about six to eight weeks out, in early November. Front-load tasks with lead times first — gift lists, shipped or personalized presents, and card orders — then save quick, in-person jobs like wrapping and baking for the final week or two when you're home anyway.

faq_items.question: What are the main categories on a Christmas planning checklist?
faq_items.answer: Six categories cover everything: gifts (list, budget, bought and wrapped), cards (addresses, ordering, mail-by date), decor (tree, lights, outdoor display), food (menu, baking, groceries), cleaning (the pre-guest reset), and a week-by-week countdown that tells you when to do each one.

faq_items.question: How do I plan Christmas without overspending?
faq_items.answer: Set one total holiday budget, then divide it across gifts, food, decor, cards, and travel before buying anything. Assign a per-person gift amount and write it next to each name, shop big-ticket items during November sales, and keep receipts in one envelope for returns.

faq_items.question: How far in advance should I mail Christmas cards?
faq_items.answer: Order or make cards six to eight weeks out and aim to mail them by the second week of December so they arrive before the holiday. Keep your address list on your checklist so you're not rebuilding it from scratch every single year.

faq_items.question: Can I reuse the printable checklist every year?
faq_items.answer: Yes. Print one copy and slip it into a sheet protector to check off with a dry-erase marker, or reprint a fresh copy each year. Many people like starting each December with a blank checklist and a clean slate to fill in.
